body:
**Supersedes the patch above** (comment 6623860245, branch head `49950cb62`): your retest found a real hole in it, and this rework closes it. Thank you for testing it on the real gateway — the 404 capture is what pinned the fix. ## What's wrong with the first patch The retry treated *any* answer that wasn't 401/403 as "this header worked". Your vendor answers `x-api-key` alone with **404 `AUTH_KEY_MISSING`** — a header it doesn't take at all — so the first patch learned `x-api-key`, handed the 404 back, and left every model on the provider broken until the file was edited. The trigger was right; the learn was too wide, exactly as you said. ## The fix (patch below, 2 commits) - `RetryOneAuth` now learns only a **2xx** answer (your narrowing): a header the vendor doesn't take (404) or an outage (5xx) is not learned, and the next header is asked before the answer goes back. On your gateway: 403 → `x-api-key` alone (404, not learned) → `Authorization` alone (200) → `authHeader: "bearer"` kept — your trace, reproduced by a test. - The **model list** had the same two gaps and is fixed in the same commit: it learned on not-401/403 too, and it never retried on the #5021 403 "invalid api-key" refusal at all (only on the outright 401), so a provider on such a vendor couldn't fetch its list to begin with. It now retries on both refusals and learns only an answer. ## Verification | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | New `TestRetryOneAuth404NotLearned` (your retest trace: 403 → 404 not learned → 200 learns bearer) | red before the fix (the 404 was learned and returned), ok after | | New `TestList404NotLearned` (same vendor shape on the model list) | red before the fix (list failed outright on the 403), ok after | | Existing `TestRetryOneAuth*`, `TestBothAuthRefused`, `TestAuthKeyRefused`, `TestAuthHeaderChoice`, `TestListLearnsOneAuth` | ok | | Ablation: product files (`authheader.go`, `live.go`) back at the parent, tests kept | both new tests red | | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/provider ./internal/catalog` | ok (provider 136s, catalog 4.8s) | | `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go build ./...` | clean (known `dockflap`/`trayimage` cgo warnings only) | | `git am -3` onto current `main` (`0ee424e3e`) in a clean tree | applies clean; targeted tests pass there | ## Not verified No request against your gateway itself — the 403/404 shapes are reproduced from your curl table as test fixtures; the vendor's answers beyond that table (e.g. whether `AUTH_KEY_MISSING` ever comes with a different status) are not covered.
patch (git am applies it as is; SHA-256 first 16: e759e2dd5abb1c03 then dad674bae643ab83) ``` From 4bf9742d66c6166b7858c25ab0f71e202f695912 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: ggbdpq Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 05:38:36 +0800 Subject: [PATCH 1/2] authheader: a 403 that reads as an invalid key asks again with one header (#5021) MIME-Version: 1.0 Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit A vendor that takes one auth header alone can answer a request carrying both with a bare 403 "invalid api-key" — no word about the headers (Jasonpetrelli: Qwen-Flash 403 with both, 200 with Authorization alone; Deepseek-Flash 200 either way). The retry entered on a 401 naming both headers, so a vendor whose refusal never names them never got the second ask, and the model stayed unreachable on the Anthropic endpoint while the same key passed on Chat. AuthKeyRefused reads that shape (403, the body saying the api-key itself is invalid) and RetryOneAuth asks again with each alone beside the 401 branch; the learning pipeline is unchanged, and a 403 that says nothing of the key goes as it came. Tests: TestRetryOneAuthOnKeyRefused403 (vendor 403s both -> retry x-api-key -> ok and kept; a region 403 goes as it came, asked once), TestAuthKeyRefused (the word shapes, and 401s or other 403s not told). bytes.ToLower(body) + for _, s := range []string{ + "invalid api-key", "invalid api key", "invalid_api_key", + "invalid x-api-key", "invalid key", "无效的 api", + } { + if bytes.Contains(b, []byte(s)) { a/internal/provider/authheader_test.go b/internal/provider/authheader_test.go index bfb2857b9..2c4ba72f9 100644 --- a/internal/provider/authheader_test.go +++ b/internal/provider/authheader_test.go @@ -248,3 +248,68 @@ func TestRetryOneAuthOnlyOnThatRefusal(t *testing.T) { t.Errorf("own header asked %v", got) } } + +// #5021 (Jasonpetrelli): a vendor that takes one auth header alone can +// answer a request carrying both with a bare 403 "invalid api-key" — no +// word about the headers. Asked again with x-api-key alone it passes, and +// that is kept; a 403 that says nothing of the key is handed on as it came. +func TestRetryOneAuthOnKeyRefused403(t *testing.T) { + azureHome(t) + var mu sync.Mutex + var asked [][2]string + srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { + x, a := r.Header.Get("x-api-key"), r.Header.Get("Authorization") + mu.Lock() + asked = append(asked, [2]string{x, a}) + mu.Unlock() + if x != "" && a != "" { + w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden) + w.Write([]byte(`{"error":{"message":"relay: invalid api-key","type":"permission_error"}}`)) + return + } + w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json") + w.Write([]byte(`{"id":"msg_1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hi"}]}`)) + })) + t.Cleanup(srv.Close) + if err := Save(Provider{ID: "relay", Name: "Relay", Anthropic: srv.URL, Key: "k", Models: []string{"claude-haiku-4-5"}}); err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + p, _ := Find("relay") + rs := p.TestModels(context.Background(), []string{"claude-haiku-4-5"}) + if len(rs) != 1 || !rs[0].OK { + t.Fatalf("test: %+v", rs) + } + mu.Lock() + got := append([][2]string(nil), asked...) + mu.Unlock() + if len(got) != 2 || got[0] != [2]string{"k", "Bearer k"} || got[1] != [2]string{"k", ""} { + t.Errorf("asked %v", got) + } + if q, _ := Find("relay"); q.AuthHeader != AuthXAPIKey { + t.Fatalf("kept %q", q.AuthHeader) + } + + // a 403 that says nothing of the key goes as it came, asked once + var mu2 sync.Mutex + var asked2 [][2]string + srv2 := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { + x, a := r.Header.Get("x-api-key"), r.Header.Get("Authorization") + mu2.Lock() + asked2 = append(asked2, [2]string{x, a}) + mu2.Unlock() + w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden) + w.Write([]byte(`{"error":{"message":"region not served"}}`)) + })) + t.Cleanup(srv2.Close) + if err := Save(Provider{ID: "relay2", Name: "Relay2", Anthropic: srv2.URL, Key: "k", Models: []string{"claude-haiku-4-5"}}); err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + q, _ := Find("relay2") + q.TestModels(context.Background(), []string{"claude-haiku-4-5"}) + mu2.Lock() + got2 := asked2 + mu2.Unlock() + if len(got2) != 1 { + t.Errorf("region 403 asked %v", got2) + } +} -- 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155) ``` ``` From bb9ac0fc8022e8a4f52d6ac7e1e2ae882ba33b01 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: ggbdpq Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:43:43 +0800 Subject: [PATCH 2/2] authheader: a header a vendor doesn't take is not one that worked (#5021) MIME-Version: 1.0 Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit The reporter's retest of the #5021 retry found the learn too wide: any answer that wasn't 401/403 counted as the header working. Their vendor answers x-api-key alone with a 404 saying the apiKey header is missing — a header it doesn't take at all — so the retry learned x-api-key, handed the 404 back, and every model on the provider 404'd from then on. Only a real answer is learned now (2xx): a header the vendor doesn't take (404) or an outage (5xx) is not, and the next header is asked before the answer goes back. The model list had the same two gaps: it learned on not-401/403, and it never retried on the #5021 403 "invalid api-key" refusal at all — only on the outright 401 — so a provider on such a vendor could not fetch its list to begin with. It now retries on both refusals and learns only an answer. Fixes #5021 (reporter Jasonpetrelli's retest and 2xx narrowing; the 404 vendor shape and capture are theirs). err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + p, _ := Find("relay") + rs := p.TestModels(context.Background(), []string{"claude-haiku-4-5"}) + if len(rs) != 1 || !rs[0].OK { + t.Fatalf("test: %+v", rs) + } + mu.Lock() + got := append([][2]string(nil), asked...) + mu.Unlock() + if len(got) != 3 || got[1] != [2]string{"k", ""} || got[2] != [2]string{"", "Bearer k"} { + t.Errorf("asked %v", got) + } + if q, _ := Find("relay");
